title: Checkpoint: Brain and Nerves
objective: After this level you can explain how nerves and the brain sense, decide and act.
summary: The nervous system senses, integrates and responds, like a batter judging a pitch. The brain doing it is about 2 percent of your weight but uses about 20 percent of your energy.

cards.headline: Chapter 6 finale: your brain is the body's priciest organ.
cards.body: It's about 2 percent of your weight and uses about 20 percent of your energy. First, one baseball pitch that puts this whole chapter to work. Then, what the bill says.

cards.headline: Sense, decide, act
cards.body: The nervous system has three basic jobs: sensation, integration and response. Watch a batter. Sensory neurons carry news of the pitch in. Then comes integration: the ball's speed and path get weighed against memories and the game situation. A batter doesn't swing automatically. Only then does the response go out, as motor messages down the spinal cord and along the nerves to the muscles. Or the bat stays still.

cards.fact: Your brain: about 2 percent of your weight, about 20 percent of your energy.
cards.context: That's for an adult at rest, and the rate is remarkably steady. Solving a hard puzzle adds only a tiny amount on top of that large baseline. So thinking harder won't burn much extra; the brain is expensive even when you're just sitting there.

mascot.line: Pricey, yes. But it just ran a whole chapter on itself, which is a neat trick.

cards.headline: Chapter 6 complete
learned: Brain and spinal cord decide; nerves carry news in and orders out
Neurons: electrical along the axon, chemical across the synapse
Reflexes loop through the spinal cord before you feel the pain
Hippocampus files memories; sleep stages cycle through the night
The brain: about 2% of your weight, about 20% of your energy

questions.prompt: Brain and Nerves recap: about what share of the body's energy does an adult brain use at rest?

options.label: About 2 percent
options.rationale: That is its share of body weight.

questions.explanation: The brain is about 2 percent of body weight but uses about 20 percent of the energy the body consumes at rest.

questions.prompt: Brain and Nerves recap: a batter weighs the pitch's speed and the game situation before swinging. Which job is that?

options.label: Sensation
options.rationale: Sensation is taking in the pitch in the first place.

options.label: Response
options.rationale: The response is the swing that follows.

questions.explanation: Integration is weighing incoming information against memories and circumstances before a response is chosen.

questions.prompt: Brain and Nerves recap, from Level 55: which statement matches what brain research shows?

options.label: Creative people run on the right hemisphere
options.rationale: No one had a stronger side overall.

options.label: The hemispheres do identical work
options.rationale: Speech leans left for most people.

options.label: Some jobs lean to one side, but people are not left- or right-brained
Logical people run on the left hemisphere
options.rationale: The scans found no such people.

questions.explanation: Some functions, like speech, lean to one hemisphere, but the 2013 Utah study found no one with a stronger side overall.

questions.prompt: Brain and Nerves recap, from Level 56: what did Ebbinghaus's forgetting curve show?

options.label: Forgetting happens at an even pace
options.rationale: It is steep at first, then slows.

options.label: Forgetting is fastest soon after learning
Nothing is forgotten in the first week

questions.explanation: Ebbinghaus found forgetting is fastest soon after learning and then slows.

questions.prompt: Brain and Nerves recap, from Level 57: which sleep stage is the deep sleep with the slowest brain waves?

options.label: REM
options.rationale: REM brain waves are close to waking.

questions.explanation: Stage 3 non-REM is deep sleep, with the slowest brain waves, when you may be hard to wake.
